title: Make a concept map you can correct
goal: Turn a technical description into a labelled flow without confusing order and causation.
explanation: A hierarchy and a process flow are different diagrams. Ask which relationship each arrow represents, and include alternate or failed paths. Start with a small verified account instead of asking a model to draw the entire internet from memory. A neat diagram can still have the wrong order.
sampleInput: Source sketch: A browser may use a cached address or ask DNS for a server address. It then establishes the needed connection and sends an HTTPS request. A server returns a response. The browser renders content and may request more resources. DNS failure can stop the normal path.
prompt: Turn the sketch into a text flow with labelled arrows. Include the cached-address branch and DNS-failure branch. Distinguish “next step” from “part of.” Do not imply DNS downloads the webpage or that one response always completes rendering.
workedExample: Browser → cached address? yes → connect/request; no → DNS lookup → address found? yes → connect/request; no → show error/retry. Response → render → possibly request images/styles. DNS resolves names; it does not serve the page content.

steps.title: Identify entities and actions
steps.text: Make separate lists for browser, DNS, server and response steps.

steps.title: Generate the text map
steps.text: Request labelled arrows and both alternate/failure paths.

steps.title: Trace one success
steps.text: Walk from typing an address to first rendering; point to every required stage.

steps.title: Trace one failure
steps.text: Follow DNS failure without pretending a response was received.

steps.title: Redraw and explain
steps.text: Use the visual guide as a model and write a plain-language description of one arrow’s exact meaning.

checks: DNS resolution is distinguished from sending or receiving webpage content.
The cache and failure branches are present.
Each arrow has a stated relationship rather than an unexplained decorative connector.
commonMistakes: Confusing a list of components with an ordered process.
Removing error branches to make the diagram look simpler.
offline: Write steps on cards and arrange a flow with a cache branch and failure branch.
reflection: Which arrow would mislead a beginner if it had no label?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. DNS resolution is distinguished from sending or receiving webpage content.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. The cache and failure branches are present.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Confusing a list of components with an ordered process.
